steps.claim: §3.4 requires sequential small-step execution and says every executed instruction pushes a run-history frame (§7.4). §4.1 store.i8 writes one byte to its live allocation. Thus after the legal sequence n=1572864; p=alloc n; hostcall; z=const.i8 0; store.i8 p z; ret, with a full reply of 0xa5 bytes, successful completion must leave memory[1]=0 and retain all six instructions. A reported host limitation is not an ISA instruction that may silently advance past the store. The R21/R22 reported-resource reading permits refusal with the full prefix preserved, not a hidden execution-state change.

That allocation fails again and exits before assigning undo.control. No HistoryFrame is pushed. The advanced ip consequently escapes with the resource Err. S0 core: normal reported resource rejection leaves a state that is not the retained sequential prefix, and a retry produces a successful completion that omitted the specified store. Both verdicts must remain revise. This finding fits no stated INV-1..6 theorem: INV-6(C), specifically 1.7.6, concerns checker-domain host outcomes, not CC memory transactions; T4 assumes a valid retained trace. Whole-run reversal passes here and is not alleged broken. The round-22 request-clone and name-coverage fixes remain resolved; this is a separately exposed sparse-COW failure path, not evidence that either exact old witness still fails.

Prepare/perform fallible memory work transactionally before committing control, or retain the pre-instruction memory owner and restore it without allocation on failure. step increments ip before executing the row. save_bytes records the old byte; Memory::store then attempts fallible sparse copy-on-write/growth. On error, step calls undo_record(undo)? before returning the original error. The new undo_record starts by preparing sparse capacity again whenever undo.bytes is nonempty, even though no store byte changed. That reservation also fails, so it exits before assigning undo.control. At 1 MiB the shared copy can fit but geometric growth cannot; 1.25/1.5 MiB controls also reproduce the failure when the shared copy itself is denied.

Drop the held observer and call step_once again: the next op is load.i8, not the rejected store.i8. run completes with Int(64,1), byte [1], fault=None. At 256 MiB the same program/probe executes the store, adds its frame and returns Int(64,2), byte [2], fault=None. Both children exit 0 and whole-run reversal subsequently restores entry. Thus successful reversal later does not detect the skipped forward operation.

S0 core: fallible shared-memory preparation has introduced a failed rollback that consumes an unexecuted store and permits a wrong successful continuation. This fits no stated INV-1..INV-6 theorem: INV-6 concerns checker labels/resources, not CC store rollback; ISA T4 assumes a valid retained trace and does not justify skipping a forward instruction. The two original R22 blockers can be resolved while this new defect still prevents core and whole-crate acceptance.
